newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus says suspends Adelaide cable roll-out.
newsitem.headline: Optus says suspends Adelaide cable roll-out.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Friday it had suspended its cable rollout for local telephony and pay-television services in Adelaide to focus on marketing in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.
A spokeswoman said the decision also would allow Optus to investigate "commercially favourable" alternatives for providing the Adelaide service, including the use of third parties.

"The network roll-out in the other areas we are building - Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane - has been largely completed and in those areas we are moving into a very strong marketing phase," she told Reuters.

"Because Adelaide was not at that same stage of development, what we are looking at now are a number of options we have for alternative ways to complete the build and still offer those services," she said.
"We do not know how long (those investigations will take) and we do not know what the outcome might be," she said.

The spokeswoman said Optus, which is 49 percent owned by British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless Plc, had rolled out about 2,000 km of supportive strand around Adelaide but very little cable itself.
The roll-out had been suspended as of today, with 76 staff positions made redundant, she said.
